newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels slaughter 30 people in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels slaughter 30 people in Algeria.

text.p: Moslem rebels slaughtered 30 people, including two babies and seven women, overnight at Chebli village in Blida province 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, Algerian security officials said on Thursday.
The massacre took place hours before the start of a three-week campaign for June 5 parliamentary elections.

Among the 30 people "assassinated in a cowardly way" -- the term used by Algerian authorities when Moslem rebels cut the throats of their victims -- were 17 children, two babies and seven women, the security forces said in a statement reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.
It was the latest massacre in Algeria. Moslem guerrillas, in the worst mass killing in the five years of violence, killed 93 villagers in nearby Medea province late in April.

About 60,000 people have been killed in strife pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
